subtopics.title: The State in the Market — Taxes, Subsidies and Price Controls

questions.question: A tax on a product, such as the levy on sugary drinks, causes:
options: Supply to shift LEFT and upward by the tax — higher price, smaller quantity, burden shared between buyer and seller
Supply to shift right — lower price, larger quantity
Demand to shift right — higher price, larger quantity
No change, since sellers absorb all taxes

questions.question: Zero-rating staples like brown bread, maize meal and rice while most goods carry fifteen percent VAT works like:
options: A price ceiling on food
A subsidy-style cheapening of the poor household's basket — supply-side relief that lowers price and raises quantity
A price floor protecting farmers
A tax that shrinks the staples market

questions.question: A maximum price pinned BELOW equilibrium produces:
options: A surplus the state must buy up
Immediate market clearing
A permanent SHORTAGE — quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied — with queues, rationing and black markets following
Higher quality goods

questions.question: The two-handed argument about the minimum wage is that it:
options: Helps employers and harms all workers
Has no effect on any market
Only affects government employees
Lifts the earnings of workers who keep jobs, while a wage set above market-clearing can reduce how many workers firms hire

subtopics.title: From Barter to Industry — the Evolution of Markets

questions.question: The five stages of market evolution in order are:
options: Self-sufficiency; surplus and barter; money; government enters; industrialisation
Money; barter; industry; government; self-sufficiency
Barter; industry; money; self-sufficiency; government
Government; money; barter; industry; self-sufficiency

questions.question: The herder who cannot trade his goat because the grain farmer wants a plough blade illustrates:
options: A price ceiling in a rural market
The DOUBLE COINCIDENCE OF WANTS — barter requires each party to want exactly what the other offers, at the same time
Derived demand for labour
The store-of-value function of money

questions.question: Money's four functions are:
options: Saving, spending, lending, taxing
Investment, consumption, export, import
Medium of exchange, unit of account, store of value, standard of deferred payment
Coins, notes, cards, phone codes

questions.question: South Africa's entry into the industrial stage ran through:
options: A textile revolution in the coastal cities
Subsistence farming reforms
Early motor manufacturing
The MINERAL REVOLUTION — diamonds then gold pulling railways, capital and workers inland, and entrenching migrant labour

subtopics.title: Population, Labour and the Rules of Work

questions.question: The labour force contains:
options: Everyone aged fifteen to sixty-four who is employed, plus those unemployed AND actively seeking work
The entire population between fifteen and sixty-four
Only people in formal employment
Everyone including learners, retirees and the discouraged

questions.question: Demand for labour is called DERIVED demand because:
options: It is calculated from official statistics
A firm hires only because customers demand what the workers produce — the bakery hires because bread sells
It derives from trade union pressure
Wages are derived from profits

questions.question: The three anchor statutes matched to their jobs are:
options: All three set minimum wages
All three regulate strikes only

Basic Conditions of Employment — the floor under every contract; Labour Relations — the collective contest of unions, strikes and lock-outs; Employment Equity — fairness and redress in hiring and promotion
They apply only to the public sector

questions.question: The dispute ladder climbs in the order:
options: Labour Court, then arbitration, then conciliation
Strike first, then negotiate
Arbitration, then conciliation, then bargaining
Bargaining; CONCILIATION at the CCMA; ARBITRATION with a binding ruling; the Labour Court for questions of law

questions.question: The unemployment rate is calculated as:
options: The unemployed divided by the LABOUR FORCE — never by the whole population
The unemployed divided by the total population
The employed divided by the unemployed
The labour force divided by the working-age population

questions.question: A retrenched mineworker whose skills fit no growing sector near his home has which type of unemployment, needing which remedy?
options: Frictional — faster job adverts
STRUCTURAL — education, retraining and shrinking the distance between people and work
Seasonal — off-season alternatives
Cyclical — waiting for the upswing

questions.question: Redress organised through the four factors of production means:
options: Taxing each factor at the same rate
Nationalising land, labour, capital and enterprise
Land restitution, redistribution and tenure; employment equity and skills for labour; broad-based ownership and finance for capital; small-business support for entrepreneurship
Replacing all four factors with imports

questions.question: "Judge every programme by the livelihood it leaves, not the object it hands over" warns that:
options: Programmes should never transfer assets
Objects are more valuable than livelihoods
Only cash transfers count as redress
Land without finance, a qualification without a vacancy, or a tender without working capital each falls short unless the support arrives with the instrument

questions.question: The referee image teaches that the state's four moves in a market are:
options: Tax to shrink a market, subsidise or zero-rate to widen one, pin a ceiling to protect buyers, pin a floor to protect producers
Print money, borrow, spend, tax
Ban, license, inspect, fine
Import, export, save, invest

questions.question: "Ceilings make queues" because at the pinned-down price:
options: Sellers offer more than buyers want
Buyers multiply while sellers shrink back — and the gap becomes queues, rationing and a side door of illegal higher prices
The market clears instantly
Quality improves so demand falls

questions.question: "Floors make piles" refers to:
options: Ceilings set above equilibrium
Taxes collected in warehouses
A minimum price above equilibrium leaving a surplus that somebody must buy, store or export
Queues outside shops

subtopics.title: From Swapping Goats to Swiping Cards

questions.question: Sipho walks home with his goat because the grain farmer wants a plough blade, not a goat. Barter failed because:
options: The double coincidence of wants was missing — no partner wanted exactly what he offered while offering exactly what he wanted
The goat was priced too high
The river blocked the trade
Money had lost its value

questions.question: Money's four jobs in the story are:
options: Coin, note, card, code
The go-between, the measuring rod, the storage jar, the promise-keeper
Tax, spend, save, borrow
Mint, guard, weigh, build

questions.question: Buying now and paying at month-end is possible because money serves as:
options: A medium of exchange only
A unit of account only
A standard of DEFERRED PAYMENT — debts can be written down and settled later
A store of value only

questions.question: After money, the two newcomers who arrive as markets grow are:
options: Banks and insurers
Unions and bargaining councils
Importers and exporters
The STATE — minting, enforcing, taxing, building — and then the MACHINES of industrialisation, which in South Africa were pulled inland by diamonds and gold

subtopics.title: The Gate, the Team and the Starting Line

questions.question: At the factory gate, the granny on pension and the classmate still in school are:
options: Outside the labour force — not counted as unemployed
Unemployed by the strict definition
Discouraged work-seekers
Part of derived demand

questions.question: "The factory hires when its orders grow, never before" restates:
options: The minimum wage rule
DERIVED demand — the demand for labour follows the demand for what labour produces
The double coincidence of wants
The expanded definition of unemployment

questions.question: "The queue is really five queues wearing one face" means:
options: Unemployment statistics are unreliable
All unemployment has a single cause and cure
Frictional, structural, cyclical, seasonal and technological unemployment stand together but each needs its own remedy
Only five people are unemployed at any gate

questions.question: "The field without seed money is still not a farm" argues that redress instruments:
options: Should avoid transferring land
Work automatically once legislated
Are unnecessary where laws are equal
Each need their partner support — finance, skills, market access — before an asset becomes a livelihood
